svg.title: Svalbard circuit-block schematic and approximate placement
svg.desc: Explicit RF I and Q mixer, gain, filter and converter paths; PLL feedback loops; wired equalizer, sampler, CDR and serializer; programmable analog tiles; references and host control. All external terminals are at the perimeter. Intended circuits, not a completed transistor schematic.

g.text: Proposed connectivity with RF west, wired east, clocks north and digital south
RF OR WIRED PAYLOAD ACTIVE — not simultaneous
Shared services; further analog / clock sharing under evaluation
RF RX — I AND Q ARE SEPARATE CIRCUITS
RF TX — SEPARATE I/Q RECONSTRUCTION AND MIXERS
Local bidirectional path; detail on final sheet
Idle gates driver bias; detect current senses the output load
I/Q queues · capture / playback · update sequencing
SPI · calibration · atomic run / stop · fault / epoch recovery
Wired words / GPIO PHY / clock alignment
Queues · raw/bypass · DDR capture / launch · local HOST_A / HOST_B rails
Symbols: G/A = gain/error amplifier; × = mixer; Σ = sum; ∫ = integration; ± = comparator; D/Q = sampling latch.
Differential pairs and digital words use bundled lines. Junction dots connect; crossings without dots do not. Purple: clocks. Orange: reference. Blue: control.
Panel service ports distribute configuration, bias and supply locally to their enclosed circuits. No implied global analog crossbar. This is not a transistor netlist or layout.
7 SUPPLY / RETURN PAIRS → LOCAL DOMAIN FEEDS
CONNECTION DETAILS / REPEATED CHANNELS AND SHARED SERVICES
Named ports are connections to the overview. I and Q instances are independent; these are intended circuit interfaces.
SAR ADC × 2 — ONE INSTANCE PER I / Q CHANNEL
SAR_STEP requires a local conversion clock; its implementation and rate remain to be qualified.
DAC × 2 — ONE INSTANCE PER I / Q CHANNEL
Underrun / idle selects a configured safe code; mode changes invalidate pending words.
RF · wired · clocks · analog · digital · host
Supply/return bundles are distinct nets; local regulation is conditional, not an assumed qualified LDO.
INTERFACE CONNECTION REGISTER — BUNDLES EXPANDED BY FUNCTION
ADC-I/Q → result valid + sample words → RX queues → formatter → D2H DDR launch → D2H_D[9:0], D2H_CLK
H2D_D[9:0], H2D_CLK → DDR capture → deframer → TX queues → I/Q shadow latches → DAC_UPDATE → DAC arrays
Slicer → sampler → deserializer → RX queue → D2H; H2D → TX queue → serializer → main + delayed taps → line driver
SCLK, CS_N, MOSI → register/control engine; status/readback → MISO; RESET_N → reset synchronization → local state resets
Registers → gain / filter tuning / mux select / divider ratio / current trim / termination / driver taps / idle / enables
PLL lock / reference present / CDR status / queue flags / detect result / comparator result → synchronized status → SPI / host framing
Buffered selected analog source → tile / monitor mux → RF-I diagnostic selector → I ADC; tile comparator → calibration / status
RF and wired VCO → programmable feedback divider → PFD → charge pump → R–C loop filter → VCO; CDR phase feedback is separate
Connectivity intent, not electrical signoff: bus widths, clock-domain synchronizers, switch circuits and analog component values require schematic refinement.
TRANSPORT WIRING / CLOCK DOMAINS / LOCAL SERVICE CONNECTIONS
Arrows show transfer direction. DATA includes valid; blue reverse paths carry ready / credit. Named nets join sheets without extra pins.
FOUR CONTINUOUS STREAMS — EXPLICIT ROUTING AND CDC
CLK-HOST-TX → scheduler / packer / launch / forwarded D2H_CLK
Source clocks: ADC_RESULT for RF; CLK-RX for wired.
Sources cannot be backpressured at the analog input: overflow records a fault / discontinuity; queue sizing and host service remain requirements.
HOST TO ANALOG — DEMULTIPLEX, BUFFER, CONSUME
CONTROL / MEMORY / CALIBRATION — SEPARATE REQUEST AND RETURN
gain / RC / mux / bias / divider / idle
I/Q offset trims · clock bank · frontend settings
*Memory requests from SPI / RX capture / TX playback are arbitrated.
Capture: RF / wired RX taps → memory. Playback: MEM_TX_RF / WIRE.
RF CLOCK ACQUISITION — COUNT, COARSE TUNE, FINE LOOP
Search: hold pump; qualified bank → enable fine PLL
Initial acquisition candidate; live coarse retune / recenter circuitry remains open.
LOCAL NET MAP — THESE ARE INTERNAL CONNECTIONS, NOT ADDITIONAL EXTERNAL TERMINALS
RF VCO → quadrature buffers → separate RX-I, RX-Q, TX-I, TX-Q mixer LO ports.
Reference-derived timing → conversion step, ADC sample, DAC update, host launch; RESET_N / fault → local reset release.
Per-island latches → gain cells, filter switches, offset actuators, diagnostic selectors, termination, driver bias / tap weights.
Buffered amplitude / idle / local comparator → monitor selection → I ADC or calibration comparator → valid / result status.
Core logic, FIFO / memory, configuration / calibration and pad pre-drivers; dedicated feed and return.
A: data[4:0], SPI/reset pads. B: data[9:5], host clocks. Separate output-driver feeds / returns.
Two wired analog feed / return pairs; local RX/TX allocation and rail continuity require physical closure.
RF: RF frontends, baseband and converters. PLL: clock / master references. Local bias / reference buffers isolate loads.
Wiring is architectural intent: CDC primitives, transistor-level switching, exact widths / values and physical supply isolation are not yet closed.
LOCAL CIRCUIT WIRING / DIFFERENTIAL NETS AND FEEDBACK
Repeat each I/Q sheet twice. P and N are separate conductors; identical net names join sheets. Proposed implementation interfaces.
RX BASEBAND × I/Q — MIXER OUTPUT TO THE ADC INPUT
Local bias: TIA, PGA, filter and buffer each receive IBIAS_RX and VCM. Each active differential stage needs its own common-mode control.
TX BASEBAND × I/Q — HELD DAC CODE THROUGH RECONSTRUCTION TO RF
I or Q LO; current output
I mixer + Q mixer → differential current sum → RF driver
RF_TX_P/N; driver enable / bias / amplitude sense
Two-biquad reconstruction is a mathematical candidate. Realization, tuning range, op-amp bandwidth, Q, noise and headroom remain open.
WIRED LANE — EXPLICIT CLOCK, DATA, DETECTION AND LOOPBACK PORTS
normal RX / TX data; quiet only
TX: word FIFO → serializer (CLK_TX) → main / delayed current taps → differential output driver → WIRE_TX_P/N.
TX electrical idle disables output drive; receiver detection uses its own stimulus and sense path. CLK_TX and recovered CLK_RX are independent.
LOCAL SERVICES — INDIVIDUAL CONTROL AND RETURN CONNECTIONS
Both ADCs / paired DAC update latches
Local bias input of each active circuit
Clock gates / FIFO epochs / safe outputs
RF amplitude, TX load, bias sense (selected)
Monitor mux → I ADC or comparator
Status CDC → SPI and host event formatter
Names with commas list separate nets, not shorted conductors. Buses retain separate bits; clocks require local buffering; supply returns are not signal returns.
Full block-level connection intent. Device sizing, analog switch topology, RC values and extracted wiring remain subsequent schematic/layout work.
RF OUTPUT / PAIRED UPDATES / POWER AND BIAS WIRING
Connection detail supplements the placement overview. Ports repeat existing internal nets; no additional package terminals.
RF CURRENT SUM → DRIVER → PADS; SEPARATE LO AND MONITOR CONNECTIONS
Pre-switch tap; output / dummy switches are expanded on the isolation sheet below.
PAIRED DAC COMMIT — INDIVIDUAL DATA, SHARED TIMING, RETURN ACKNOWLEDGEMENT
Invalid epoch / missing partner inhibits commit; fault handling selects the declared safe output state.
LOCAL POWER AND BIAS — REPEAT PER DOMAIN; SUPPLY AND RETURN ARE DISTINCT WIRES
VDD top / VSS bottom; repeated fanout
Repeat for CORE, HOST_A, HOST_B, WIRE_A, WIRE_B, RF and PLL. No implicit connection between separately named VDD rails.
Circuit-block connectivity proposal; device topology, component values, resource conflicts and electrical verification remain schematic work.
OUTPUT ISOLATION / SHARED ADC — CONNECTED CANDIDATE WIRING
Expands the RF driver-to-pad path above. Switches, dummy load and readout buffer remain circuit candidates.
RF OUTPUT: DISTINCT P/N SWITCHES, INTERNAL DUMMY LOAD AND PRE-SWITCH OBSERVATION
switch controls; preserve analog charge on stop
Run: output on / dummy off. Quiet calibration: output off / dummy on.
Transition ordering, feedthrough, dummy matching and stored-charge settling require verification.
Differential lines remain distinct. Dummy termination is across DUM_P/N with a separate common-mode bias; it is not a short to VSS.
DETECTOR READOUT: SHARED I ADC, RESOURCE OWNERSHIP AND SEPARATE RESULT ROUTING
same I converter as RF RX
request I ADC; wait grant / settle
RESULT → next trial / verify / commit; completion releases ADC ownership
Single-ended detector-to-differential ADC mapping needs gain / common-mode conditioning in the readout buffer. Q ADC remains separate.
Sample demand loads the existing reference network. Mux resistance, charge injection, buffer settling and ADC kickback are not ideal wires.
Shared ADC blocks concurrent I-channel RX during calibration. Abort discards pending results; continuous detector and network charge remain.
Architectural connection intent, not a verified electrical netlist. All named buses represent separate conductors; crossings without junction dots do not connect.
CLOCK / REFERENCE / BIAS DISTRIBUTION — EXPLICIT RECEIVING PORTS
Internal sheet connections use identical net names. Separate output routes preserve independent clocks, bias nets and reference conductors.
RF LO: ISOLATE MIXER LOADS FROM THE SYNTHESIZER
RX I and Q switching mixers
TX I and Q switching mixers
Each slash-separated name is a separate clock net: this fanout denotes connectivity, not shorted I/Q phases.
CONVERTER TIMING: DISTINCT SAMPLE, DECISION AND COMMIT EVENTS
I and Q SAR state machines
I and Q active DAC code latches
CONVERTER REFERENCE: BUFFERED RESERVOIR AND SWITCHED LOADS
I and Q SAR capacitor-array reference switches
I and Q DAC reference / current-setting cells
Kelvin sense intent; return is VREF_N
BIAS AND COMMON MODE: SEPARATE LOCAL MIRRORS / BUFFERS
separate RF / BB / wired / PLL loads
LNA, mixers, RF output driver and LO buffers
PGA, filters, ADC input buffers and CMFB amplifiers
Wired CTLE, slicers, line driver, VCO and charge pumps
RESET / QUALIFICATION / FAULT RETURN — CONTROL WIRES CLOSE THE LOOP
Local reset synchronizers → all digital domains
RF / wired output and dummy-switch controls
ADC mux, DAC commit and queue controls
lock / reference loss / overflow / calibration done
Control bundles contain independent signals. Reset release is synchronized per destination clock; analog startup remains a separate circuit obligation.
These connections complete service routing at circuit-block granularity. Component pins, values and parasitics require the subsequent electrical schematic.
Same 50 terminals as the overview. Named destinations join existing sheets; no additional external test or bias pins.
ANALOG TERMINALS — EACH P AND N CONDUCTOR REMAINS INDEPENDENT
separate P and N signal ports
ESD return path; not a signal termination
separate P and N signal ports
ESD return path; not a signal termination
separate P and N signal ports
ESD return path; not a signal termination
separate P and N signal ports
ESD return path; not a signal termination
RF matching / baluns and wired channel coupling are board-side, mode-dependent networks. ESD topology and loading remain to be selected.
FAST HOST PORT — TEN REPEATED DATA WIRES AND A SEPARATE FORWARDED CLOCK
Launch Q → pads; same source forwards clock
Input/output domain boundary blocks are conditional on chosen voltages. IO supplies feed pad circuits; CORE feeds transport logic. No direct clock-domain short.
CONTROL / REFERENCE TERMINALS — INDIVIDUAL SIGNAL ROUTES
RF PLL / wired PLL / timing reference
SPI register requests / readback cross into CORE through explicit handshake mailboxes (see control sheet); SCLK is not a core clock.
Seven supply/return pairs connect to the domain distribution sheet. Board decoupling and on-die reservoirs return to their corresponding VSS.
Connection intent only: pad-cell selection, level-shifter requirements, ESD clamps, electrical values and physical routing remain unqualified.
Named ports join earlier sheets. Circuit candidates below expand boxes; values and topology selection remain open.
WIRED PLL — PFD, PUMP, TWO-CAP FILTER AND INTEGER-EDGE FEEDBACK
RF and wired PLLs are separate instances with separate storage, VCO outputs and feedback nets.
RF three-cap candidate: see expanded sheet below for R3, C3, centering shunts and acquisition controls.
LOCAL ANALOG TILE — BOUNDED INPUT SELECTION, WEIGHT, INTEGRATION AND OBSERVATION
Reset switches discharge each integration capacitor; the controller applies RESET_INT_P and RESET_INT_N together.
Integrator outputs also feed the local comparator / sample path shown in the overview. The diagnostic mux is a bounded local route.
Local selection and weight programming do not imply a global RF crossbar. Tile count, switch circuits and legal modes remain to be fixed.
Lines show intended electrical connectivity; this is not yet a complete transistor netlist or an LVS-qualified schematic.
Candidate circuit connectivity; isolated mathematical lock evidence is not transistor or full-chip qualification.
RF INSTANCE ONLY — SEPARATE PUMP, SLOW STORAGE AND VCO TUNING NETS
coarse search → settle → fine acquire → qualify
phase error, count error, node bounds
VCP / VSLOW / VTUNE sensing: explicit wiring on final sheet
N[k] programming / divider timing: explicit wiring on final sheet
Values are from the balanced mathematical candidate; tolerances, physical capacitance and noise remain unqualified.
RF VCO output branches to divider, coarse counter and LO drivers; none of these destinations is a second oscillator.
Window sensing and PFD observation are intended high-impedance taps, not loads qualified by these mathematical tests.
RECENTERING — THREE INDEPENDENT FINITE DISCHARGE BRANCHES
VBIAS_CENTER — finite buffered centering reference, not a fourth storage node
Each branch uses Rcenter × Cnode ≈ 200 ns; switch resistance and reference impedance must be included in circuit refinement.
Sequencer: hold pump → enable all shunts → wait / check → disable shunts → coarse settle → enable fine pump.
The model stores voltage offsets about the operating point. Physical VBIAS_CENTER and headroom are still to be chosen.
LOCAL SUPPLY CONDITIONING — OPTIONAL REGULATOR CIRCUIT CANDIDATE, REPEATED ONLY WHERE REQUIRED
Amplifier compensation, pass-device polarity and stability versus load / CLOCAL require circuit design; direct supply bypass remains an option.
Named ports join the existing sheets without extra package pins. Analog feedback, clocks and control buses are distinct nets.
RF PLL — RATIO PROGRAMMING, NODE SENSING AND ACQUISITION INTERLOCKS
Programming bus ≠ clock: modulus changes occur at a defined divider boundary. Circuit timing remains to be qualified.
Qualification logic — synchronized observations, counters and explicit bounds
VCP_IN_RANGE, VSLOW_IN_RANGE, VTUNE_IN_RANGE, PFD_ERROR, REF_COUNT, REF_PRESENT
Local services: window comparators use VDD_PLL / VSS_PLL and finite buffered thresholds; logic uses its own supply domain.
Named ports are identical nets across sheets, not extra IOs. Sense input capacitance, offset, loading and synchronization remain design work.
Interlock requires CENTER_EN low before enabling the pump; centering and active phase correction must not contend.
This expands candidate block connectivity. It does not assert completed transistor wiring, noise closure, or a fabricated implementation.
CURRENT RF CANDIDATE — ONE LOADED NETWORK FOR PAD, CALIBRATION AND LOOPBACK
RF active mode; wired payload disabled. Experimental connectivity, not completed transistor circuitry or a scaled layout.
does not recover absolute pad gain
COMMITTED CORRECTION → DAC CODE PATH; no attenuation normalization
LOOPBACK FROM PAD; finite network state
RF_RX_P/N front end OR loaded pad
Each I/Q filter: two second-order sections + one real pole; circuit realization remains open.
ADC / DAC charge loads; gain and oscillator coupling
RC values label mathematical assumptions. Differential conductors are bundled here; no additional external terminals.
Pad observation reads PAD_P/N directly. Detector reads the pre-switch MONITOR_P/N node; these are not the same net.
Output-off / dummy-on switching retains capacitor state. Quiet calibration uses relative-gain fitting, with explicit commit.
Still open: loaded waveform quality, driver current / supply limits, transistor realization, package and parasitic qualification.
OPERATING POLICY — ONE CHIP, RF OR WIRED ACTIVE; SHARE PHYSICAL RESOURCES
stop → isolate → release → configure → settle → qualify
RF TX/RX + required local clock / analog services
full-duplex lane; TX clock and independent RX CDR
Share host interface, memory, calibration, reference / bias and diagnostic services
Evaluate one retunable TX PLL and reusable analog tiles; preserve each mode’s timing and electrical requirements
Additional sharing is encouraged. Separate RF/wired front ends remain provisional; switch loading, tuning range and noise need evidence.
Existing separate PLL / front-end sheets show candidate structures, not a requirement to duplicate every physical resource.
No extra IOs are introduced. Existing pin and bandwidth allocations remain provisional until exclusive-mode rebudgeting.
Behavioral ownership and handovers tested; physical / RTL interlocks remain open. Concurrent traffic is optional stress.
This policy supersedes earlier simultaneous-operation requirements; both capabilities remain required on the first fabricated chip.
CONFIGURABLE CIRCUITS — SHARED PADS, LOCAL TIMING AND RF CHANNEL CONTEXTS
Design intent: generic resource controls and electrical branches still require full RTL / circuit qualification.
USB mode: WIRE_TX high-Z; no serial AC coupling on D+/D-.
FPGA board sidebands: USB VBUS switch / sense; DP AUX transceiver / HPD. No extra chip terminals.
keep LO warm during packet exchange
RF LO + LPF/PGA + ADC/DAC + TX/RX gates
existing local RF paths; no additional RF chain
RF: HE20 Wi-Fi / LE / BR-EDR / O-QPSK / LoRa. Independent waveform, hopping and turnaround gates.
Serial: 0.480–2.50 Gb/s; video x10 fractional references; HD-SDI 1.485 and 1.485/1.001 Gb/s (external coax).
One resource configuration; DP one RBR lane; RF one 20 MHz stream. 50 terminals, 12.92 mm² allocation ceiling.
Shared-pad capacitance and FPGA response latency are feasibility gates, not assumptions of successful support.
HDMI / DVI — THREE IDENTICAL SINGLE-LANE DIES
Board assembly, not extra lanes on the 1x1 die. Source shown; sink reverses data direction.
host FIFO > serializer / sampler > DC pad
REF_IN / x10 word clock / phase control
host FIFO > serializer / sampler > DC pad
REF_IN / x10 word clock / phase control
host FIFO > serializer / sampler > DC pad
REF_IN / x10 word clock / phase control
Each die: 50 terminals, one wafer.space slot; RF payload off. FPGA/board owns DDC, HPD, 5 V and optional CEC.
720p / 1080p: integer and /1.001 clocks; intermediate x10 rates. Framed GPIO links; no chip protocol IDs.
Open gates: DC pad / ESD, x10 clock and word phase, cross-die skew, FIFO / CDC, independent video compliance.
